# FDG4056

> DO NOT define a nested type as a member of an interface. Many languages do not support such a construct.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.9 Nested Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG4056
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Move the type '{0}' out of the interface '{1}'

Library only: the reason is the many languages that cannot consume such a construct; an application's interfaces are used from one language. FDG4056 reports an externally visible type declared inside an interface (allowed from C# 8). Moving the type changes the public API, so there is no code fix.

## From the book

In general, use nested types sparingly, and avoid their exposure as public types.
